title: Aggressive Cows
problemStatement: Place k cows in stalls so that the minimum distance between any two is as large as possible.
intuition: If a spacing d is achievable then any smaller spacing is too — feasibility is monotone *decreasing* in d. Binary search the largest feasible d, checking greedily.

approaches.title: Brute: try every distance
Optimal: binary search on the distance
approaches.idea: Greedy placement: always take the first stall that is far enough.
approaches.time: O(n log n + n log(max distance))
approaches.dryRun:
stalls=[1,2,4,8,9] k=3, range [1,8]
d=4: place 1,8 -> 2 cows, fail
d=2: 1,4,8 -> 3 cows ok
d=3: 1,4,8 -> 3 cows ok, ans=3
d=4 already failed -> 3
approaches.whyWorks: Placing each cow as early as possible leaves the most room for the rest — an exchange argument.

complexity.time: O(n log n + n log D)

edgeCases: k = n -> the minimum adjacent gap
commonMistakes: Forgetting to sort the stalls first
Flipping the feasibility direction (this one maximises, so move lo up on success)
patternRecognition: "Maximise the minimum" / "minimise the maximum" -> BS on answer + greedy check
followUps: Minimise the maximum distance to gas stations (#103)
Prove the greedy check is exact
interviewInsight: Note the direction flip versus Koko: here success moves lo up. Mixing the two templates is the usual bug.
